topic: TriviaQA exact match performance: Extractive Reader vs. Generative RAG

verified_evidence.P1: RAG-Sequence achieves 56.8 EM on standard open-domain split, 68.0 EM on TQA-Wiki split (Table 1, Physical/Printed p. 6). Explicitly acknowledges DPR 57.9 in §4.1.
verified_evidence.P2: DPR Multi achieves 57.9 EM (Single 56.8 EM) on TriviaQA test set (Table 4, Physical p. 8).

conclusion: Extractive reader holds a modest 1.1-point advantage on standard open-domain split where answers are concise extractable spans, but RAG-Sequence dominates by +7.5 points on TQA-Wiki split.

topic: WebQuestions exact match: REALM (40.7) vs. T5-11B+SSM (44.7)

verified_evidence.P3: REALM (330M parameters) achieves 40.7 EM on WebQuestions (Table 1, Physical p. 7).
verified_evidence.P1: T5-11B+SSM achieves 44.7 EM on WebQuestions (Table 1, Physical/Printed p. 6).

conclusion: Non-comparable due to 34x parameter disparity (11.3B vs 330M), T5 supervised multi-task pre-training on 100k+ SQuAD reading comprehension examples, and entity-targeted Salient Span Masking (SSM).

topic: Retrieval Frequency and Utility: Adaptive Retrieval vs. Unconditional Always-Retrieve

verified_evidence.P1: Standard RAG unconditionally retrieves top-k documents for every query (§2.1, Physical/Printed p. 3).
verified_evidence.P4: Unconditional retrieval degrades Llama2-7B accuracy on PubHealth from 34.2% to 30.0% due to noisy context, whereas Self-RAG adaptive retrieval achieves 72.4% (+42.4 points) (Table 2, Physical/Printed p. 8).

conclusion: Controlled ablations prove that always-retrieving hurts performance when retrieval is unnecessary or misleading, confirming the empirical advantage of selective, self-reflective retrieval.
